subject.title: [Feature]: Cron job output routing — hard-coded destination for job results (file, channel, session)

question: Should OpenClaw add a framework-owned cron output target contract for files, channels, and sessions, and what safety, fallback, and status semantics should it use?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested fix adds public cron config plus security-sensitive file writes, recipient routing, and session-state mutation that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Design unified output targets
options.body: Define one `output` or equivalent cron contract that covers file, channel, session, silent, fallback, audit, status, and docs before implementation.

options.title: Narrow to delivery defaults first
options.body: Defer file and session injection, and solve only the less broad channel/default-target repetition in the focused delivery-default issue.

options.title: Decline framework routing
options.body: Keep cron output routing explicit through prompts, tools, webhooks, or plugins, and document that no scheduler-owned file/session routing will be added now.

recommendation.title: Design unified output targets
recommendation.body: Define one `output` or equivalent cron contract that covers file, channel, session, silent, fallback, audit, status, and docs before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is the strongest combined signal from recent cron default/config history and the prior maintainer-facing triage on related cron delivery issues.
